## Overview

This document simulates a clinical trial dataset with missing values.

The dataset contains participant-level information, including study design data (study site, randomization arm), some demographic and anthropometric variables (sex, age, height, weight), lifestyle factors (physical activity), and the clinical outcome (cure).

Specifically, it creates the two datasets used in the `mice` demo (`04_mice_demo.qmd`):

1. **`data_complete`**: a synthetic randomised trial with no missing values, including the participants' BMI (`bmi`).
2. **`data_missing`**: a copy of `data_complete` with `bmi` removed and missing values introduced under a **missing at random (MAR)** mechanism.

Both datasets are saved as `.RData` files.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(glue)
theme_set(theme_light())

n <- 200 # number of participants
set.seed(999)
```

## Part 1: The complete dataset

### Data-generating process

```{r}
sim_pars <-
  list(
    study_sites = c("A", "B", "C"),
    sex = c("F", "M"),
    age_range = c(18, 80),
    ht_mean = c(F = 166, M = 180),
    ht_sd = 7,
    ht_decline_age = 60,
    ht_decline_per_year = 0.1,
    physical_activity_levels = c("low", "med", "high"),
    physical_activity_probs = c(0.35, 0.40, 0.25),
    physical_activity_probs_site_A = c(0.15, 0.35, 0.50),
    physical_activity_probs_site_C = c(0.6, 0.25, 0.15),
    bmi_median = c(low = 30, med = 24, high = 18),
    bmi_sd_log = 0.05
  )
```


We simulate the variables one after the other, so that each one can depend on the ones simulated before it.

```{r}

sim_tbl <- tribble(
  ~Variable             , ~`Simulation specifications`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       ,
  "`study_site`"        , glue('{toString(sim_pars$study_sites)} with equal probability')                                                                                                                                                                                                    ,
  "`arm`"               , '1:1 randomisation to `"placebo"` or `"treatment"`'                                                                                                                                                                                                                ,
  "`sex`"               , '`"F"` or `"M"` with probability 0.5 each'                                                                                                                                                                                                                         ,
  "`age`"               , glue("Uniform between {sim_pars$age_range[1]} and {sim_pars$age_range[2]} years (whole years)")                                                                                                                                                                    ,
  "`ht`"                , glue("Normal, mean {sim_pars$ht_mean['M']} cm (M) or {sim_pars$ht_mean['F']} cm (F), ", "SD {sim_pars$ht_sd} cm, with a {sim_pars$ht_decline_per_year} cm/year decline ", "after age {sim_pars$ht_decline_age}")                                                   ,
  "`physical_activity`" , glue('`"low"`, `"med"`, `"high"` with probabilities ', '{toString(sim_pars$physical_activity_probs_site_A)} at site `"A"`, ', '{toString(sim_pars$physical_activity_probs_site_C)} at site `"C"`, ', 'and {toString(sim_pars$physical_activity_probs)} otherwise') ,
  "`bmi`"               , glue("Log-normal distribution depending on physical activity level, with median ", "{sim_pars$bmi_median['low']} (low), {sim_pars$bmi_median['med']} (med) or ", "{sim_pars$bmi_median['high']} (high) kg/m², and SD {sim_pars$bmi_sd_log} on the log scale")      ,
  "`wt`"                , "bmi × (ht / 100)², in kg"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         ,
  "`cure`"              , "Bernoulli, with the probability given by the logistic model below"
)


sim_tbl |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = everything()) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(1), color = "black"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = c(2, 8))
  )
```

The probability of cure follows a logistic model:

$$
\text{logit}\,  P(\text{cure} = 1) = \beta_0 + \beta_\text{trt}\, \text{trt} + \beta_\text{wt}\, (\text{wt} - 80)\, \text{trt} - \beta_{\text{age}} \, (\text{age} - 50)
$$

where "trt" is 1 for participants in the treatment arm. 

```{r}
#| label: true-parameters
beta_0 <- qlogis(0.30) # placebo, BMI = 26
beta_trt <- log(2.5) # treatment effect
beta_wt <- log(0.95) # per weight unit
beta_age <- 0.1 # per year of age
```



### Simulation

```{r}
#| label: simulate
data_complete <-
  tibble(id = sprintf("P%03d", 1:n)) |>
  mutate(
    study_site = sample(sim_pars$study_sites, n, replace = TRUE) |> factor(),
    sex = sample(sim_pars$sex, n, replace = TRUE) |>
      factor(levels = sim_pars$sex),
    age = round(runif(
      n,
      min = sim_pars$age_range[1],
      max = sim_pars$age_range[2]
    )),
    ht = rnorm(
      n,
      mean = if_else(sex == "M", sim_pars$ht_mean["M"], sim_pars$ht_mean["F"]) -
        sim_pars$ht_decline_per_year * pmax(age - sim_pars$ht_decline_age, 0),
      sd = 7
    ),
    physical_activity = {
      pa <- character(n)
      site_a <- study_site == "A"
      site_c <- study_site == "C"
      pa[site_a] <- sample(
        sim_pars$physical_activity_levels,
        sum(site_a),
        replace = TRUE,
        prob = sim_pars$physical_activity_probs_site_A
      )
      pa[site_c] <- sample(
        sim_pars$physical_activity_levels,
        sum(site_c),
        replace = TRUE,
        prob = sim_pars$physical_activity_probs_site_C
      )
      pa[!(site_a | site_c)] <- sample(
        sim_pars$physical_activity_levels,
        sum(!(site_a | site_c)),
        replace = TRUE,
        prob = sim_pars$physical_activity_probs
      )
      factor(pa, levels = sim_pars$physical_activity_levels)
    },
    bmi = exp(rnorm(
      n,
      mean = log(case_match(
        physical_activity,
        "low" ~ sim_pars$bmi_median["low"],
        "med" ~ sim_pars$bmi_median["med"],
        "high" ~ sim_pars$bmi_median["high"]
      )),
      sd = sim_pars$bmi_sd_log
    )),
    wt = bmi * (ht / 100)^2,
    arm = sample(rep(c("placebo", "treatment"), length.out = n)) |>
      factor(levels = c("placebo", "treatment")),
    p_cure = plogis(
      beta_0 +
        beta_trt * (arm == "treatment") +
        beta_wt * (wt - 80) * (arm == "treatment") -
        0.1 * (age - 50)
    ),
    cure = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p_cure)
  ) |>
  mutate(across(c(ht, wt, bmi), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  select(id, study_site, sex, age, ht, wt, bmi, physical_activity, arm, cure)

data_complete
```

### Summary and visualization of simulated data

```{r}
#| label: summary-numeric
data_complete |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    across(c(age, ht, wt, bmi), \(x) round(mean(x), 1), .names = "mean_{.col}")
  ) |>
  gt()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-activity-by-site
#| fig-cap: "Physical activity by study site."
data_complete |>
  ggplot(aes(x = study_site, fill = physical_activity)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(x = "Study site", y = "Proportion of physical activity levels")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bmi-activity
#| fig-cap: "BMI by study site."
data_complete |>
  ggplot(aes(x = study_site, y = bmi, col = study_site)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, varwidth = TRUE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Study site", y = "BMI (kg/m2)")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-wt-by-site
#| fig-cap: "Weight by study site."
data_complete |>
  ggplot(aes(x = study_site, y = wt, col = study_site)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, varwidth = TRUE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Study site", y = "Weight (kg)")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-wt-vs-ht
#| fig-cap: "Weight versus height by study site."
data_complete |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ht, y = wt, col = study_site)) +
  geom_point(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Height (cm)", y = "Weight (kg)")
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-ht-by-site
#| fig-cap: "Height by study site."
data_complete |>
  ggplot(aes(x = study_site, y = ht, col = study_site)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, varwidth = TRUE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(x = "Study site", y = "Height (cm)")
```

```{r}
#| label: cure-rates
data_complete |>
  group_by(arm, sex) |>
  summarise(n = n(), cure_rate = mean(cure), .groups = "drop") |>
  gt()
```

```{r}
data_complete |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = wt, y = cure, col = arm) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "glm",
    method.args = list(family = "binomial")
  )
```


## Part 2: The dataset with missing values

### Missingness mechanism

We remove `bmi` (it is typically a "calculated variable" and not a raw measurement) and introduce missing values as follows:

-   **Study site**: at sites A and B, the baseline probability that `age`, `ht`, `wt` or `physical_activity` is missing is 10%. At site C it is 30%.
-   **wt**: is more likely to be missing than the other variables and probability also depends on the study site
-   Study design and outcome variables (`id`, `study_site`, `arm` and `cure`) are never missing.

Because missingness depends only on the study site (which is always observed), the data are **missing at random (MAR)**.

```{r}
#| label: missingness-parameters
p_miss_site <- c(A = 0.10, B = 0.10, C = 0.30)
p_miss_wt <- c(A = 0.1, B = 0.1, C = 0.9)
```

```{r}
#| label: introduce-missingness
# Draw one missingness indicator per participant and variable
add_missing <- function(x, p) if_else(runif(length(x)) < p, NA, x)

data_missing <-
  data_complete |>
  select(-bmi) |>
  mutate(
    # Probability of missingness based on study site and variable-specific effect for wt
    p_miss = p_miss_site[as.character(study_site)],
    across(c(age, ht, physical_activity), \(x) add_missing(x, p_miss)),
    wt = add_missing(wt, p_miss_wt[as.character(study_site)]),
  ) |>
  select(-p_miss)


data_missing |>
  head(10) |>
  gt(caption = "First 10 rows of the dataset with missing values") |>
  # highlight missing values by coloring them
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "lightpink"),
    locations = map(
      colnames(data_missing),
      \(col) cells_body(columns = all_of(col), rows = is.na(.data[[col]]))
    )
  )
```

### Checks

Proportion of missing values per variable:

```{r}
#| label: missing-per-variable
data_missing |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) mean(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "prop_missing")
```

Proportion of missing values per variable and study site:

```{r}
#| label: fig-missing-by-site
#| fig-cap: "Proportion of missing values by study site."
data_missing |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(sex, age, ht, wt, physical_activity),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_transform = as.character
  ) |>
  group_by(study_site, variable) |>
  summarise(prop_missing = mean(is.na(value)), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = prop_missing, fill = study_site)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion missing", fill = "Study site")
```

Number of missing values per participant:

```{r}
#| label: fig-missing-per-participant
#| fig-cap: "Number of missing values per participant."
data_missing |>
  mutate(n_missing = rowSums(is.na(pick(everything())))) |>
  count(n_missing) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_missing, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Number of missing values", y = "Number of participants")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-wt-vs-cure
#| fig-cap: "Scatter plots of weight vs cure for complete and missing data."
library(patchwork)
data_complete |>
  filter(arm == "treatment") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = wt, y = cure) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(col = study_site)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial")) +
  xlim(range(data_complete$wt) + c(-1, 1)) +

  data_missing |>
    filter(arm == "treatment") |>
    ggplot() +
  aes(x = wt, y = cure) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(col = study_site)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial")) +
  xlim(range(data_complete$wt) + c(-1, 1)) +

  plot_layout(ncol = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-wt-vs-cure-overlay
#| fig-cap: "Scatter plot of weight vs cure for complete and missing data (in green)."
data_complete |>
  filter(arm == "treatment") |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = wt, y = cure) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(col = study_site)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial")) +
  geom_smooth(
    data = data_missing |> filter(arm == "treatment"),
    method = "glm",
    method.args = list(family = "binomial"),
    col = "green",
    fill = "green"
  ) +
  xlim(range(data_complete$wt) + c(-1, 1))
```




## Export & Session info

```{r}
#| label: export
save(data_complete, file = "simulated_data/data_complete.RData")
save(data_missing, file = "simulated_data/data_missing.RData")
```

The files `data_complete.RData` and `data_missing.RData` are saved in the `simulated_data/` directory.
